\section{Professional Summary}
Visionary technologist with over four decades of experience in systems that
the industry has bravely moved on from. Recognized authority on keeping
mission-critical fax machines alive, coaxing data off 5.25-inch floppies, and
explaining to executives why the mainframe in the basement \emph{cannot}
simply be ``unplugged for a second.'' Fluent in COBOL, Morse, and the subtle
body language of a dot-matrix printer about to jam.

\section{Experience}

\role{Chief Legacy Officer}{Consolidated Widgets \& Telegraph Co.}{1998 -- Present}{Peoria, IL}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Kept a 1983 mainframe in continuous operation for 27 years using
        spare parts sourced from three estate sales and one very confused museum.
  \item Reduced fax transmission failures by 64\% by installing a dedicated
        phone line and asking everyone to stop standing on the cord.
  \item Successfully migrated the company's payroll from punch cards to
        magnetic tape in 2019, a mere four decades behind schedule.
  \item Authored the internal guide \emph{``Have You Tried Blowing On It?''},
        now in its eleventh printing.
\end{itemize}

\role{Senior Floppy Disk Whisperer}{DataSafe Archival Solutions}{1989 -- 1998}{Dayton, OH}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Recovered 14,000 corrupted spreadsheets from disks that had been
        used as coasters, bookmarks, and on one occasion, a door wedge.
  \item Pioneered the ``gentle shake'' method for unsticking 5.25-inch
        disks, later adopted as a regional best practice.
  \item Trained 40 junior technicians in the ancient art of write-protect
        tab management.
\end{itemize}

\role{Modem Acoustics Specialist}{BaudCo Telecommunications}{1984 -- 1989}{Akron, OH}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Diagnosed connection problems purely by listening to handshake
        tones, with a reported accuracy of 97\%.
  \item Achieved a then-record 2400 baud connection during a thunderstorm.
  \item Was asked to stop humming the handshake in the break room.
\end{itemize}

\role{Junior Telegraph Operator}{Midwestern Wire \& Signal}{1979 -- 1984}{Toledo, OH}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Transmitted over 200,000 messages, only three of which were
        accidentally the lyrics to a popular song.
  \item Introduced the office to the concept of ``STOP'' as punctuation
        and as a lifestyle.
\end{itemize}



\section{Notable Projects}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Project Rewind (2004):} Built a climate-controlled vault for
        the company's VHS training library, including the beloved 1987
        classic \emph{Lifting Boxes Safely: The Musical}.
  \item \textbf{Operation Beige Box (2011):} Restored 32 beige desktop towers
        to working order, each named after a member of the 1985 office
        bowling team.
  \item \textbf{The Great Y2K Non-Event (1999):} Spent New Year's Eve in the
        server room with a flashlight, a thermos, and a laminated backup
        plan. Nothing happened. Takes full credit.
  \item \textbf{Fax-to-Email Bridge (2016):} Engineered a system in which
        incoming emails are printed, faxed to the next room, and scanned
        back in, ``for the paper trail.''
\end{itemize}
